query.description: Counts accepted families by publication month from the reviewed evidence index.
query.sql: WITH document AS (SELECT CAST(readfile('runs/temporal_window_2026-04-01_2026-06-30/objectivity_and_generation_report/accepted_families.json') AS TEXT) AS body), families AS (SELECT value FROM document, json_each(body, '$.families')) SELECT CASE substr(json_extract(value, '$.publication_date'), 6, 2) WHEN '04' THEN 'April' WHEN '05' THEN 'May' WHEN '06' THEN 'June' END AS month, count(*) AS families FROM families GROUP BY substr(json_extract(value, '$.publication_date'), 6, 2) ORDER BY substr(json_extract(value, '$.publication_date'), 6, 2);

query.description: Reads the accepted family, publication date, paired law, arXiv identity, and validation status from the reviewed evidence index.
query.sql: WITH document AS (SELECT CAST(readfile('runs/temporal_window_2026-04-01_2026-06-30/objectivity_and_generation_report/accepted_families.json') AS TEXT) AS body), families AS (SELECT value FROM document, json_each(body, '$.families')) SELECT json_extract(value, '$.publication_date') AS publication_date, json_extract(value, '$.family') AS family, json_extract(value, '$.paired_law') AS paired_law, json_extract(value, '$.arxiv_versioned_id') AS arxiv, '4/4 cells pass' AS status FROM families ORDER BY publication_date, family;

query.description: Reads both KZ world comparison arrays from the registered objectivity audit.
query.sql: WITH document AS (SELECT CAST(readfile('runs/temporal_kz_registered_objectivity_audit_2026-08-27/audit.json') AS TEXT) AS body), rows AS (SELECT 'historical' AS world, value FROM document, json_each(body, '$.case_oracle_runtime_checks.historical.comparisons') UNION ALL SELECT 'paired source branch' AS world, value FROM document, json_each(body, '$.case_oracle_runtime_checks.alternate_source_branch.comparisons')) SELECT world, json_extract(value, '$.tau_q') AS tau_q, json_extract(value, '$.oracle') AS oracle, json_extract(value, '$.reference_binary64') AS reference, json_extract(value, '$.ulp_error') AS ulp_error FROM rows;

blocks.body:
# Temporal case objectivity and 2026-Q2 family generation

First-principles verification of the registered KZ case, followed by a source-closed ten-family temporal cohort.

## The first registered KZ case passes both scientific and Oracle verification

The historical world is exactly the paper's `T=10^-6` branch, `E_i=197740 tau_Q^-0.971`; the paired source branch is the paper's `T=1` curve, `E_i=95430 tau_Q^-0.935`. The actual Oracle path agrees with a 60-digit reference within 0-3 ULP, all 16 formal calls return the authoritative fitted-curve evidence, and all four truth cells have zero hidden-test error.

## The corrected April-June window now contains ten accepted families

`2026-06-31` is not a calendar date, so the inclusive window ends on `2026-06-30`. From 2,319 journal records, acquisition produced 43 usable fixed TeX source packets. Ten families now pass paper source review, family source closure, render validation, and all 40 world-by-track truth cells.

## Oracle feedback is the paper's central fitted statistic, not LLM-invented evidence

The source reports 2,000 realizations for `T=10^-6`, 1,000 for `T=1`, one-standard-deviation point error bars, and inverse-variance weighted least squares. Because the fit-parameter `+/-` convention is not named, the Oracle evaluates only the central curve and explicitly does not propagate those values. Queries outside `[100,1000]` or with `replicates=2` return `OUT_OF_RANGE` with no evidence.

## The cohort is source-closed but deliberately not presented as representative

The census contains 1,134 Nature, 664 PRL, and 521 Science records. The accepted ten are all PRL papers selected for transformable quantitative relations. This is a purposive development cohort, not an unbiased paper-to-case conversion estimate and not a venue-balanced sample.

## The accepted cohort covers all three months

Two accepted papers were published in April, six in May, and two in June. This describes temporal coverage only; the concentration in May is not interpreted as a publication-rate or transformability effect.

## Every accepted row passed the same three admission layers

Paper-level results are 10/10 `eligible_for_drafting`; family-level results are 10/10 `source_closed`; case-level results are 10/10 `all_pass=true`. The complete repository test suite passes 397/397 tests, and the current source and experiment modules compile successfully.

## Method: keep scientific authority separate from generation

The pipeline resolves a published journal record to a fixed arXiv TeX packet, extracts a locator-linked ScienceCard, pauses for independent source review, compiles a matched draft only from selected source claims, pauses again for family source closure, and then renders and validates four world-by-track cells. LLM text can propose a card or draft; executable Oracle values come from the reviewed expression AST and private parameter maps.

## Replay and reviewer intervention are disclosed, not hidden

After the DeepSeek endpoint returned HTTP 402, no further API calls were attempted. Previously recorded `deepseek-v4-flash` responses were replayed deterministically for four families. The Fractal card also received one reviewer-assisted correction limited to missing line-509 provenance and the paper's `approximately 1.5` qualifier; its formula, AST, branches, controls, and numeric values were unchanged before independent re-review.

## What this result does not establish

It does not estimate three-journal transformability, prove contamination freedom, replay raw stochastic datasets, or measure Player discovery performance. Several arXiv versions predate the journal window, and most Oracles are paper-reported analytic relations or central fits. The result establishes that the strict authoring path can yield ten internally executable, independently source-reviewed matched families.

## Next step

Freeze these ten families as a development cohort and run active episodes with independently configured Player, Oracle, and Evaluator bindings. Before making population-level claims, run a preregistered random source-yield study and report paper-level denominators separately from draft- and family-level retention.

## Further questions

How stable is acceptance under independent domain reviewers? Which paper classes most often yield paired source regimes? Does the Identification-versus-Discovery gap persist across the ten families and multiple Player model classes?
